findings.title: Two-zone mode "auto" is always on: finish-now and questionnaire entries are planned as two-zone houses
findings.claim: An entry created by Finish setup now (no zone value saved) or by the building questionnaire (never asked the two-zone question) runs the two-zone model, because ThermalParameters.from_config treats the default mode 'auto' exactly like 'on'.
findings.mechanism: thermal_model.py:1122 tests `two_zone_mode in (TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON, DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE)`; DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE is 'auto', so the presence rule in the else branch (the documented meaning of auto: 'two-zone as soon as any zone value has ever been saved', and the comment two lines above) is unreachable. config_flow._derive_preset then reads that verdict through presets.preset_from_config and writes two-zone keys for every questionnaire answer, contrary to its own docstring ('derives a single-zone model').

evidence.unit: entries (finish_now entry with no zone value planned two-zone)
evidence.machine: box B13, Linux x86_64 container, 4 vCPU, shared with up to two other finder seats
evidence.contention_note: other finder seats running on the box; the number is a count/plan value, immune to load

perturbation.change: ThermalParameters.from_config wrapped so mode 'auto' (or absent) answers by zone-key presence -- the one-line fix of dropping DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE from the tuple at thermal_model.py:1122 (`two_zone_auto.py --perturb`)

findings.metric_definition: Created entries whose published two_zone_enabled is True while the entry holds no zone value and never answered the two-zone question (mode absent = auto).
findings.phenomenon_property: An entry whose two-zone mode is 'auto' (or absent) is planned two-zone exactly when it carries a zone value; a setup path that never asks the question yields a single-zone model.
findings.seam_rule: grep -n "DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE\|TWO_ZONE_MODE_AUTO" custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py  (every reader of the auto default; plus PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D17/s2/two_zone_auto.py over the create_entry paths)

null_control.note: an explicit on/off answer is honoured in both arms; only the auto default is wrong

reproduction_steps: Walk user -> user_sensors -> finish_setup -> finish_now -> setup_overview -> create_entry
Build HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator on the entry; run one cycle
two_zone_enabled is True and the plan carries upper/lower trajectories although no zone value exists
findings.proposed_fix_scope: thermal_model.py ThermalParameters.from_config: let 'auto' fall to the presence rule; re-check presets.preset_from_config / config_flow._derive_preset so a fresh questionnaire derives single-zone keys only; golden fixtures of default entries will drift.
expected_golden_drift: tests/golden coordinator fixtures built from entries without two_zone_mode (coord_minimal and similar)

findings.title: The outdoor temperature sensor never reaches the plan while a weather forecast exists
findings.claim: With a forecast available, the plan's current-hour outdoor temperature and its energy are identical whether the configured outdoor sensor reads -25, -3 or +10 C, although the field is documented as beating the forecast for the current hour.
findings.mechanism: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._weather_series builds the plan's outdoor series from forecast rows only; the measured value (_current_state.outdoor_temperature) is used for that series only in the no-forecast fallback. The sensor feeds COP/learning and the published outdoor_temperature, not the plan.

evidence.unit: K spread of plan step-0 outdoor over sensor readings {-25,-3,+10} C
evidence.machine: box B13, Linux x86_64 container, 4 vCPU, shared with up to two other finder seats
evidence.contention_note: other finder seats running on the box; the number is a count/plan value, immune to load

perturbation.change: _weather_series wrapped so the current hour's four quarter steps take the measured outdoor temperature (`outdoor_sensor.py --perturb`)

findings.metric_definition: Max-min over sensor readings {-25,-3,+10} C of the plan's step-0 outdoor temperature (and of planned space kWh), forecast fixed at -5 C.
findings.phenomenon_property: When an outdoor sensor is configured and fresh, the plan's current hour is planned at the measured outdoor temperature rather than the forecast's.

null_control.note: with no forecast the same harness sees the sensor reach the plan, so the zero is the forecast path, not the rig

findings.proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._weather_series (or _forecast_arrays): override or bias the current hour with a fresh outdoor reading; or, if the plan deliberately ignores it, D6 rewords strings.json and docs/configuration.md:87.

findings.title: Quick setup's wood furnace and wood-tank probe change nothing in the plan of the plant quick setup creates
findings.claim: On an entry made by quick setup with wood furnace and wood buffer tank answered yes and the top probe picked, the planned energy is identical with the furnace on or off and the probe at 85 or 35 C, because the two-tank model also requires a throttling mixing valve the quick path never asks for.
findings.mechanism: ThermalParameters.topology_layout returns no_valve whenever mixing_valve_mode is not throttling, so wood_tank_configured (the probe) never selects two_tank_4way; the external-heat detector is enabled only by the separate options switch external_heat_detection_enabled (default False), so 'stand the pump down while the fire is lit' never happens either. quick_setup._quick_setup_schema's docstring calls the probes 'the two-tank model's own gate'. Grid cells (4, printed individually by the harness, below the five-cell leave-one-out threshold): all four 21.6738 kWh; leave-one-out spread 0.0.

evidence.unit: kWh spread of planned space energy over furnace{on,off} x probe{85,35} C on the quick-setup entry
evidence.machine: box B13, Linux x86_64 container, 4 vCPU, shared with up to two other finder seats
evidence.contention_note: other finder seats running on the box; the number is a count/plan value, immune to load

perturbation.observed_value: valve_arm_plan_kwh_spread=11.805 kWh (furnace on, probe 85 C: 5.65 kWh vs probe 35 C: 14.90 kWh)

findings.metric_definition: Max-min of planned space kWh over the 2x2 grid furnace{on,off} x wood-probe{85,35} C on an entry created by the quick-setup path.

findings.title: The night-mode schedule kept on the setup pre-fill page caps nothing
findings.claim: A pump night-mode schedule kept on the config flow's device pre-fill page leaves the plan at full nameplate power inside it, because the companion power fraction defaults to 1.0 and the setup page never offers it.
findings.mechanism: silent_mode.compose/caps return no cap when silent_mode_power_fraction >= 1.0 (DEFAULT_SILENT_MODE_FRACTION=1.0); the setup pre-fill page writes silent_mode_windows only, so the stored schedule is inert until the user finds the fraction on the options grid page.

evidence.unit: kW change of the max planned power inside the kept 06-10 UTC window
evidence.machine: box B13, Linux x86_64 container, 4 vCPU, shared with up to two other finder seats
evidence.contention_note: other finder seats running on the box; the number is a count/plan value, immune to load

perturbation.change: config: silent_mode_power_fraction=0.6 stored beside the kept schedule; code: `silent_prefill.py --perturb` reads the fraction as 0.6 when a schedule is stored at the 1.0 default

findings.metric_definition: Max planned kW inside the kept night window with the schedule minus without it, the window being the horizon's only cheap stretch.
findings.phenomenon_property: A night-mode schedule the setup flow stores reduces the power the plan counts on inside it.

null_control.note: the same plan does cap once a fraction is stored, so the zero is the missing fraction

findings.proposed_fix_scope: config_flow device_prefill (offer or default the fraction with the schedule) or silent_mode (a stored schedule with no fraction caps at a documented default).

findings.title: The setup pre-fill page stores its After-saving navigation choice in the entry's data
findings.claim: Submitting the config flow's device pre-fill page writes the navigation field after_save ('menu' or 'close') into the created entry's data, where no reader uses it.
findings.mechanism: async_step_device_prefill keeps every non-empty submitted key (`saved = {k: v for k, v in _flatten_section_input(user_input).items() if v not in (None, '')}`) and the shared _prefill_schema carries after_save with a default; the options flow pops the key instead.

leads.what: With a day-selector spec 'weekdays 06:00-08:30, weekend 08:00-09:30', on Saturday 07:00 UTC the published dhw_in_demand_window is True, dhw_next_window_in_hours 0.0 and dhw_windows '06:00-09:30' (the flat union, params.dhw_demand_windows), while the plan uses the weekend window opening 08:00. Entity attributes misreport per-day windows.

Same root as D17-s2-01 seen from the option: the options page's 'Automatic' (strings.json options.step.thermal_model_zones two_zone_mode, docs/configuration.md:1075 'two-zone as soon as any zone value has ever been saved') behaves as On.

The options grid page's silent_mode_windows is documented (docs/configuration.md:1171) as stopping the plan counting on full power, but with silent_mode_power_fraction at its 1.0 default it caps nothing (D17-s2-04's mechanism on the options axis).
wood_furnace_enabled on does not enable the external-heat detector; external_heat_detection_enabled defaults False, so 'stand the pump down while the fire is lit' needs a second option.
Kept from the setup pre-fill page they land in the entry; their effect on the writes was not measured here (options/write axis).

Says the plan aims for the comfort temperatures and the target is the climate reference, yet target 21->22 moves the solved plan (optimizer.py reads config.target_temp in fallbacks/held reference/baseline): sentence vs code, a D6 item.

'Saving a hot water time frame here turns hot water planning on' omits that an explicit 'no hot water tank' answer (quick setup writes dhw_enabled False) wins: measured 0.0 kWh after keeping a window. D6 wording.
